chunks: Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah narrated from Uthman ibn Isa from Sama'ah who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'Indeed, I saw Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, mention riba (usury) in more than one verse and magnify it.' He said, 'Do you know why?' I said, 'No.' He said, 'So that people would not refrain from doing good deeds (or acquiring wealth through permissible means).'.
ai.seo_question: Why did Allah mention usury in multiple verses but not all verses?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) elucidates the divine wisdom behind the selective mention of riba in the Quran, noting that its absence in every verse prevents excessive fear from paralyzing people's engagement in permissible commerce and good deeds. This reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on *wasatiyyah* (moderation), ensuring that the prohibition of riba does not become a barrier to economic activity and social benevolence.
